title: I Applied the Escape-Room Hint Cap to the Host Who Sold Extra Clues

parts.text: I booked the 7:10 p.m. room and the laminated cap on the desk said: TWO HINTS. NO STAFF SELLS. The host, Glen, palmed a third card into a sleeve labeled VIP when my group stalled on the lock. I was thirty-one, birthday booker, holding a receipt that listed two. Glen shrugged. "Hosts are players of atmosphere." I photographed the sleeve, the cap, and the POS line. Then I asked for the hint log. At 7:24 the owner pinged why Glen's name was on a sold-clue ticket. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The owner can see Glen's VIP sleeve on the hint log with the cap he laminated.

social.video_title: He sold a third hint under a VIP sleeve — Part 1/2
social.description: Escape room, a host's sleeve, and a two-hint cap he posted himself. I logged the sale. Would you have asked for the hint log?

parts.text: Glen called it flavor until the birthday group asked for the receipt. I printed the ticket, the cap, and the photo. The third card went back in the wall. Glen ran the room with two like everyone else and told the next group atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word hosts use when a POS exists. Hint policy now has a second line: HOSTS ARE NOT PLAYERS OF THE CLUE. I keep two cards on a labeled hook. Glen brown-bags his jokes. The room finally looks like a puzzle, not a store. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Hint log, owner ping, and a second line on the cap. Was VIP ever a lock?
